subject: zoology
question_text: What is the need for parasites to develop special adaptations? Mention some special adaptations developed by the parasites.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.66, Star Q 183). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: The need
lines: A parasite depends on its host for food and for
shelter.
The host resists the parasite with its defence
system and with its digestive juices.
Parasites have therefore evolved special
adaptations that let them stay in the host,
resist its defences and reach a new host.
steps.why: The adaptations only make sense once the pressure is named, so the first step states the two problems a parasite meets — the host's defence system and its digestive juices.
common_mistakes: Writing that the parasite needs adaptations to move about. It needs them to stay in the host and resist its defences.
Leaving out the host's defence system, which is the reason the adaptations exist.
steps.memory_tip: Two problems for a parasite: the host's defences and the host's digestive juices.
steps.margin_note: Three short lines. State the need before listing anything.

steps.label: Attachment and covering
lines: Organs of attachment are developed, such as
hooks, suckers and the rostellum. They hold the
parasite in place inside the host.
A tough protective covering is developed.
Ascaris has a thick cuticle and Fasciola has a
tegument, which withstand the digestive juices
of the host.
Some parasites produce anti-enzymes that
neutralise the digestive juices. Example:
Taenia.
steps.why: These three adaptations answer the same problem, staying alive inside a gut that digests food, so they are grouped together with a named example each.
common_mistakes: Naming the hooks and suckers without saying what they do.
Giving no example. Every named adaptation should carry an example.
steps.memory_tip: Hold on, cover up, cancel out: hooks and suckers, cuticle and tegument, anti-enzymes.
steps.margin_note: Three named adaptations with an example each. Two lines is enough for each.

steps.label: Reproduction and lost organs
lines: A very high reproductive capacity is developed,
because only a few of the young reach a new
host. Taenia has 700 to 900 proglottids, and
each one produces about 3500 eggs.
Sense organs and organs that are no longer used
are lost, because a parasite inside a host does
not need them.
steps.why: A parasite loses what it does not use and multiplies what it does, so these two adaptations are opposite sides of the same pressure and are easiest to remember as a pair.
common_mistakes: Giving the numbers without the name. The Taenia count is the marked example.
Writing that the parasite grows more sense organs. Unused organs are lost.
steps.memory_tip: More eggs, fewer organs: reproduction goes up, unused structures go away.
steps.margin_note: Two adaptations, one with the Taenia numbers. Two short blocks.

steps.label: Life cycles and cysts

lines.text: Complex cycles, resistant cysts, changing antigens

lines: Complex life cycles with many larval stages are
developed, so the parasite can pass through more
than one host. Example: Fasciola.
Resistant cysts are formed, which survive
outside the host until a new host takes them in.
Example: Entamoeba.
The surface antigens are changed, so the host's
immune response and vaccines become less
effective. Example: Plasmodium and HIV.
steps.why: The last three adaptations all deal with reaching a NEW host and surviving the immune response, which is the second half of the problem stated at the start.
common_mistakes: Writing that the parasite escapes the vaccine. State what happens: the surface antigens change.
Naming the adaptations without examples. Fasciola, Entamoeba and Plasmodium are the named ones.
steps.memory_tip: Getting to the next host: many stages, a resistant cyst, and a changing coat.
steps.margin_note: Three named adaptations in the box, each with its example. Closing mark.

insider_note: The question has two halves and both are marked, so state the need in full before starting the list of adaptations.
